sections.name: Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.

items.text: Vertical software · What a buyer reads first
Six lines a buyer recomputes from your own records.
Retention is the meeting. What a buyer prices is the evidence behind it: who the customers are, what they signed, and what it costs to keep them.
Retention
Gross and net, by cohort
A buyer rebuilds retention from invoices, by customer cohort and by month, and compares it with the figure in your deck. The cohort that signed two years ago is the one that gets read.
Recurring revenue
What the standard counts
Annual recurring revenue excludes one-time fees and professional services, even where they recur. A buyer restates ARR to the standard before pricing it.
Deferred revenue
Billed ahead, earned later
Annual billing in advance creates a liability a buyer treats as debt-like at closing. The working capital target is set from it.
Development cost
Capitalized or expensed
Capitalized development flatters earnings and builds an asset a buyer will write off. The buyer reads the policy, then the earnings without it.
Concentration
Customers, and their customers
A buyer reads your five largest customers, then the end market those customers sell into. In vertical software, the end market is the argument.
Contracts
Term, renewal and consent
Auto-renewal, price escalators, termination for convenience and change-of-control clauses. Each one is a term a buyer counts before pricing the certainty of close.

sections.name: Five things worth fixing before a buyer prices them.

items.text: Vertical software · What to fix first
Five things worth fixing before a buyer prices them.
In order of what moves the price, from the records the review reads.
Restate recurring revenue to the standard
Pull one-time fees and services out of ARR before a buyer does. The figure gets smaller and more believable at the same time.
Rebuild retention from invoices
By cohort, by month, gross and net. If your deck says 103 percent and the invoices say 96, the invoices win.
Write the revenue recognition policy down
One page: when revenue is recognized, how multi-year contracts are treated, how deferred revenue is carried.
Document every adjustment
Owner compensation, personal expenses, one-time costs, each with the document behind it. Undocumented add-backs are removed, not argued.
List the consents
Every customer, vendor and license agreement with a change-of-control or assignment clause, and the counterparty who can say no.

sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Vertical software · Questions
Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
Is my retention figure wrong?

It is usually measured differently from the way a buyer measures it. Logo retention from a CRM and net revenue retention by cohort from invoices are different figures, and a buyer prices the second. The review rebuilds the second from your own records.
Does a services arm hurt my price?
Not by itself. What decides the price is whether the services and the software are reported apart, with their own margins. The hybrid page covers it.
What does a buyer do with capitalized development?
Reads the policy, then reads the earnings without it. If the policy is written and consistently applied, the adjustment is a conversation. If it is not, the adjustment is the buyer’s.
Will the review raise my price?
We will not promise that. It shows what your numbers support and gives you the chance to fix what they do not before a buyer prices it.
Who sees the findings?
You. Nothing reaches a buyer, an advisor or anyone else without your written permission.
